tour.name: Greece Highlights 8-Day Private Tour: Athens, Delphi, Meteora & Santorini
tour.subtitle: Eight days from the cradle of democracy to the islands with licensed guides everywhere: the Acropolis and Cape Sounion, the oracle of Delphi, the monasteries of Meteora, and three nights on Santorini with Akrotiri, its wines and the sunset in Oia.
tour.metaDescription: 8-day private Greece tour: Athens and the Acropolis, Cape Sounion sunset, Delphi, the monasteries of Meteora, and Santorini with Akrotiri, a wine tasting and the Oia sunset. Guides, private cars, ferry and 7 nights with breakfast.
highlights: The Acropolis and the Acropolis Museum with an archaeologist guide
Sunset at the Temple of Poseidon at Cape Sounion
The sanctuary of Apollo at Delphi, centre of the ancient world
The monasteries perched on the rocks of Meteora
A high-speed ferry across the Aegean to Santorini
Akrotiri, the caldera wineries and the sunset in Oia
Seven nights in central and caldera-view hotels with breakfast
tour.overview:
Greece in a week means the great monuments of the mainland and at least one island. This private journey begins in Athens with the Acropolis and a sunset at Cape Sounion, then heads north into the mountains to Delphi, where the Greeks consulted the oracle of Apollo, and to Meteora, where monasteries stand on top of giant rock pillars. You return to Athens and take a high-speed ferry across the Aegean to Santorini for three nights on the rim of a volcano.

You have a licensed guide at every site, a private car and driver on the mainland and on Santorini, a fast ferry, and seven nights in well-chosen hotels, including a room with a view of the caldera. The pace leaves time for swims, tavernas and long Greek dinners.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 8 days, 7 nights
• Start: Athens International Airport or your hotel in Athens
• End: Santorini airport or port
• Type: private tour with licensed guides, private cars and drivers, high-speed ferry; 7 nights in hotels with breakfast
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability, hotels, ferry, tickets and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; daily walks of 3 to 6 km, with steps at the sites

WHAT YOU SEE
• Athens: the Acropolis, the Acropolis Museum, Plaka and the Ancient Agora.
• Cape Sounion and the Temple of Poseidon.
• Delphi and Arachova.
• Meteora and its monasteries.
• Santorini: Akrotiri, Pyrgos, Fira, Imerovigli and Oia.

WHY THIS WORKS
Delphi and Meteora are linked in one comfortable two-day loop by car with a night in Kalambaka, and Santorini comes at the end, so you finish the trip relaxed by the sea.

WHO IT SUITS
First-time visitors to Greece, couples, honeymooners and families who want both history and an island.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer more islands, ask us to swap Meteora for two nights on Naxos or Paros; if you love ancient sites, add Mycenae and Epidaurus.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Ferries can be delayed or rescheduled by strong winds, especially the meltemi in July and August; we keep a flexible plan. Monasteries in Meteora require covered shoulders and long skirts or trousers.

days.name: Arrival in Athens and an evening in Plaka
days.description:
What to expect: a private welcome and a first evening under the Acropolis.

Your driver meets you in the arrivals hall at Athens International Airport and drives you to your hotel in the centre, about 40 minutes away. In the early evening your guide takes you for a walk through Plaka and Anafiotika, a village of island houses built on the slopes of the Acropolis, to a rooftop where you see the Parthenon lit up.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
Any time – Airport transfer.
19:00 – Evening walk in Plaka and Anafiotika.

GOOD TO KNOW
• If you arrive late, the walk moves to another evening.

INCLUDED: airport transfer, evening walk with a licensed guide.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner, tips.

Overnight: hotel in central Athens.
Meals: none.

days.name: Athens: the Acropolis, the Acropolis Museum and the Ancient Agora, then sunset at Cape Sounion
days.description:
What to expect: classical Athens with an archaeologist guide, and the most beautiful sunset in Attica.

You climb the Acropolis at the 8:00 opening to see the Parthenon, the Erechtheion and its Caryatids, and the temple of Athena Nike, then visit the Acropolis Museum and its Parthenon gallery. After lunch in Plaka and the Ancient Agora, where Socrates taught, you rest at your hotel. In the late afternoon your driver takes you down the coast road to Cape Sounion for the sunset at the Temple of Poseidon and a seafood dinner by the sea.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – The Acropolis.
10:30 – Acropolis Museum.
12:15 – Lunch in Plaka.
13:30 – Ancient Agora.
17:00 – Drive to Cape Sounion.
18:30 – Temple of Poseidon and sunset, then dinner.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Sounion timing follows the sunset of your date.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, tickets, lunch, dinner.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks, tips.

Overnight: hotel in central Athens.
Meals: breakfast, lunch, dinner.

stops.name: Temple of Poseidon
stops.description: Sunset on the cliffs of Sounion.

days.name: Delphi and Arachova, continuing to Kalambaka
days.description:
What to expect: the oracle of Apollo and a mountain drive to Meteora.

Your driver collects you early for the drive to Delphi. With your guide you walk up the Sacred Way to the Temple of Apollo, the theatre and the stadium, and see the bronze Charioteer in the museum and the round Tholos of Athena Pronaia. After lunch in Arachova, you continue north across the plain of Thessaly to Kalambaka, at the foot of the rocks of Meteora, arriving in the late afternoon.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:30 – Departure from Athens.
10:00 – Sanctuary of Apollo and the museum.
13:30 – Lunch in Arachova.
15:00 – Drive to Kalambaka (about 3 hours).
18:00 – Arrival in Kalambaka.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Bring modest clothes for tomorrow's monasteries.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Delphi tickets, lunch.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner, tips.

Overnight: hotel in Kalambaka.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

stops.name: Delphi
stops.description: The sanctuary of Apollo and the museum.

days.name: Meteora's monasteries and back to Athens
days.description:
What to expect: the monasteries in the sky with a licensed guide, then a drive back to Athens.

You visit three of the six working monasteries, such as the Great Meteoron and Varlaam, with their frescoed churches and old winch towers, see the hermit caves and the best viewpoints, and have lunch in Kastraki. In the afternoon your driver takes you back to Athens, about 4 hours 30 minutes.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Monasteries of Meteora.
12:30 – Lunch in Kastraki.
14:00 – Drive back to Athens.
18:30 – Arrival at your hotel in Athens.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Women need skirts below the knee and everyone needs covered shoulders; wraps are lent at the entrance.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, monastery entrances, lunch.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner, tips.

Overnight: hotel in central Athens.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

days.name: High-speed ferry to Santorini and a first sunset
days.description:
What to expect: a crossing of the Aegean and your first evening on the volcano.

Your driver takes you to the port of Piraeus for a morning high-speed ferry to Santorini, about 5 hours, past the islands of the Cyclades. You arrive at the port of Athinios at the foot of the cliffs, where your driver meets you and drives you up the zigzag road to your hotel with a view of the caldera. The evening is free to watch the sunset from your terrace.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
06:30 – Transfer to Piraeus.
07:30 – High-speed ferry to Santorini.
12:30 – Arrival and transfer to your hotel.
Afternoon – Free.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Ferries can be rescheduled by strong winds; we keep a flexible plan and can switch to a short flight.

INCLUDED: transfers, ferry, lunch on board or on arrival.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner, tips.

Overnight: hotel on Santorini with caldera view.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

stops.name: Santorini caldera
stops.description: Arrival on the rim of the volcano.

days.name: Santorini: Akrotiri, Pyrgos, a caldera winery and the sunset in Oia
days.description:
What to expect: the volcanic island in one day ending at sunset, with a licensed guide, private car and a wine tasting.

You visit Akrotiri, the Bronze Age town buried by the eruption of about 1600 BC, see the Red Beach, climb through the lanes of Pyrgos for a meze lunch, and taste Assyrtiko and Vinsanto wines at a winery on the caldera. You walk the cliff path from Fira to Imerovigli and end in Oia for the sunset over the blue domes.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
12:30 – Akrotiri.
15:00 – Pyrgos and lunch.
16:30 – Wine tasting.
17:45 – Fira and Imerovigli.
19:00 – Oia and sunset.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A sunset dinner in Oia can be booked on request.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Akrotiri ticket, wine tasting, lunch.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner, tips.

Overnight: hotel on Santorini with caldera view.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

days.name: Santorini at leisure, with an optional caldera cruise
days.description:
What to expect: a free day by the sea.

The day is yours: swim at the black-sand beaches of Perissa or Kamari, walk the cliff path from Fira to Oia (about 10 km), or join an optional catamaran cruise around the caldera with a swim at the hot springs of the volcano and a barbecue on board. Lunch is at a taverna of your choice from our recommendations.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
All day – Free, or optional catamaran cruise.

GOOD TO KNOW
• We can book the catamaran, a cooking class or a sunset dinner for you.

INCLUDED: lunch voucher at a recommended taverna.
NOT INCLUDED: optional cruise, dinner, tips.

Overnight: hotel on Santorini with caldera view.
Meals: breakfast, lunch.

days.name: Departure from Santorini
days.description:
What to expect: a last morning on the island and a private transfer.

After breakfast with a view of the caldera, you have free time until your driver takes you to Santorini airport or port, depending on your onward journey.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
Morning – Free time.
As needed – Private transfer to the airport or port.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Extra nights on Santorini or another island can be added.

INCLUDED: transfer.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: breakfast.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability, hotels, ferry, tickets and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is the ferry included?
faq.answer: Yes, a high-speed ferry from Piraeus to Santorini with port transfers. A short flight can replace it on request or if winds cancel the ferry.

faq.question: What kind of hotels are used?
faq.answer: Comfortable 4-star or boutique hotels: central in Athens, with a view of the rocks in Kalambaka, and with a caldera view on Santorini. Upgrades to cave suites with private plunge pools are available.

faq.question: Is the climate tax included?
faq.answer: No. Greek hotels charge a small climate resilience fee per room per night, paid at the hotel. We tell you the amounts when we confirm.

faq.question: Can we add another island?
faq.answer: Yes. Mykonos, Naxos, Paros and Crete combine well with Santorini by ferry. We can extend the trip by a few days.

faq.question: Can the route be changed?
faq.answer: Yes. We can start on the islands and end in Athens, replace Meteora with Mycenae and Epidaurus, or adapt to your flights.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the myths, the monasteries on the rocks, the ferry and the beaches. We can book family rooms.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Ancient sites and monasteries involve uneven ground and steps, and Santorini's villages have many stairs. Tell us your needs and we will adapt.

faq.question: How much walking is there?
faq.answer: About 3 to 6 km a day, with cars for all transfers.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes with grip, sun protection, swimwear, and modest clothes for the monasteries.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: May, June, September and October. July and August are hot and windy in the islands; from November to March many island hotels close.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 21 days before the tour starts; ferry and some hotel bookings may not be refundable after that. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
